rationale: Introduces TVA to pool/prune factorial RCT variants and corrects winner's-curse, with proofs, extensive simulations, and a large state-wide immunization application. Delivers clear policy recommendations. Assumptions (beta-min, K<n, homoskedasticity) and limited code/data sharing temper confidence slightly.

Questions and claims are explicit; evidence spans formal results, simulations under multiple regimes, and a large randomized rollout. Characterization of evidence and limitations (non-uniform post-selection inference, required sparsity) is accurate. Some assumptions are untested directly in the field data.

Sound design: marginal-effects lattice, admissible pooling rules, Puffer-preconditioned LASSO for support, post-selection OLS, and bias correction. Assumptions are strong but justified; robustness checks (alt lambda, bootstrap) help. Heteroskedasticity and local-to-zero gaps remain.

Provides a general, reusable procedure to select policies from large factorial designs and yields actionable results on immunization and cost-effectiveness. Adds to post-selection inference practice. Likely to influence experimental design and policy evaluation beyond this case.

Well-organized, clear definitions and assumptions, transparent algorithms and proofs, informative figures, and careful discussion of caveats. Very long and technical; some choices (penalty selection) require appendix reading but are ultimately explained.

Algorithms and simulations are described in detail; appendices give procedures. However, analysis code and data access are not clearly provided; replication would be challenging without them. Administrative data are sensitive; no packaged software released.

Targets a core global health priority; produces implementable policy bundles with quantified effects and cost per outcome. Method generalizes to other interventions with many variants. Practical guidance (winner's-curse adjustment, cost-effectiveness) aids decision-makers.

Strong methodological plus applied contribution with clear policy relevance; fits top field outlets in development/econometrics/applied statistics; possibly general-interest if framed broadly. Assumption strength and length may limit general-journal fit.

Most likely in a top field or marginal A venue (development, econometrics, applied stats, health). General-interest journals possible but less likely given technical depth and length; policy outlets also plausible.
